waterbodies.name: Manila Bay
waterbodies.scopeNote: One shared bay identity. The 2014-2015 NFRDI survey defines a Cavite stratum, but its station map has not been georeferenced. A 2020 NFRDI annual-report summary describes landed catch across eight Manila Bay sites and reports Sardinella fimbriata as 19% of the aggregate; it does not assign that taxon to Rosario Fish Port or a capture station. Neither source establishes current species presence, current bay boundaries, or municipal-water geometry. A Marine Regions named-bay polygon was used only for an exploratory OBIS query and is not an official or app boundary. A CC BY 4.0 National Museum specimen archive and its GBIF index yielded seven historical rows with sourceStateProvince=Cavite, but all seven omit locality and waterBody. The dataset description includes landing-site, market, port and nearby-sea contexts without per-record capture-origin rules, so these records are not assigned to Manila Bay or another Cavite waterbody. A 2021 EMB Island C EIS also reports a 17-row fishing-ground table (15 fish-labeled and two invertebrate rows) covering Rosario, Noveleta, and Cavite City near a proposed Manila Bay reclamation project. It is linked here only as broad historical Cavite-side bay context: row-level localities and item-specific reuse terms remain unresolved, no table names were transcribed into this repository, and no fish occurrence or whole-bay distribution is inferred.

waterbodies.name: Maragondon River
waterbodies.scopeNote: River identity only; monitored segments do not delimit the entire channel or sanctuary. A 2014 goby barcoding paper is a historical fish lead, but it reports conflicting putative species identities and has no adopted reach geometry; all three species-level claims remain held for independent review. GBIF's exact Maragondon River query returned zero rows, which does not establish fish absence. The DENR-BMB 2016 Atlas Annex 2b also lists this river under Cavite and reports multiple municipalities; these are source-era locality context only and do not delimit the channel. A 2024 primary study reports 48 juvenile Tilapia sp. sampled at upstream, midstream, and downstream Maragondon River stations in April 2023. The authors withheld species resolution due to possible hybridization and gene-pool uncertainty; this is genus-level historical evidence only. It does not establish current presence, catchability, full-river coverage, salinity, or geometry. A 2018 sampling study published in 2019 labels fish samples Oreochromis niloticus, but this review found no independently verifiable specimen identifier or diagnostic identification protocol and no item-specific reuse license. A 2024 study reports Tilapia sp. and withholds species resolution; keep the earlier species-level claim held and do not resolve it to O. niloticus. DENR-EMB CALABARZON indexed monitoring information reports that Maragondon River was included in monitoring in 2018 and that its first-half 2020 sampling was conducted in January and February; the indexed source lists Class C. Exact station locations, measurements, and a link between any station and Gapan/Sapang were unavailable. This is historical water-quality context only, not current safety, fish evidence, or channel geometry. The 2024 provincial profile reports a 35.6 km source-described river route and Manila Bay/Ternate receiving context; this is not a surveyed channel trace or fish evidence.

waterbodies.name: Noveleta Mangrove Area

waterbodies.name: Lawa ng Tres Cruzes
waterbodies.scopeNote: BMB 2019 lists "Lawa ng Tres Cruses" in Tanza as Water Storage (15.65 ha); Cavite's 2024 profile and NIA also document Tres Cruzes Dam / irrigation infrastructure in Tanza. The source-era BMB row is not yet proven to describe the exact same impoundment as the dam records; no reported area, dam point, or boundary is adopted. GBIF CoL XR Actinopterygii exact-name and source-spelling waterBody/locality text screens returned zero; this is not evidence of fish absence. No fish assertion, salinity, current extent, access, or public admission is established.

waterbodies.name: Taal Lake
waterbodies.scopeNote: Freshwater identity context only; no complete fish list, safety or fishing-access approval. The 2021-2022 Sardinella tawilis diet study supports one attributed natural-diet guide for Taal Lake only, not a whole-lake species inventory or presence elsewhere. Three historical CAS preserved-specimen records dated 1931 and 2011 provide explicit Lake Taal and source-locality text for three species-level assertions; CONTINENT_INVALID flags are retained and coordinates are withheld. These records do not establish current presence or a complete inventory. Mutia et al. (2025) review historical Midas cichlid landed catches, but its CC BY-NC 4.0 scope and eight-versus-nine municipality mismatch remain held; no catch or municipal-presence claim is projected. A 2026-10-24 exact-field screen of four queries in the CC BY 4.0 National Museum GBIF dataset returned zero; this bounded discovery result is not evidence of absence. Two additional GBIF coordinate-envelope specimen candidates crosswalk to Taal localities only through FishBase catalog-number matches; missing GBIF locality fields, unresolved institution-code provenance, and FishBase's CC BY-NC 4.0 terms keep both held pending primary-catalog and reuse review.

waterbodies.name: Pansipit River
waterbodies.scopeNote: Four 1933 CC0 Field Museum specimen records support four historical species-locality assertions by exact Pansipit River text. All carry institution/collection quality flags; three also carry recorded-date mismatch flags. Their shared coordinate has no uncertainty and is withheld. No exact reach, estuary, salinity, current presence, or complete river list is inferred. The river links Taal Lake to Balayan Bay; one salinity class cannot be assigned to every reach from this connection. The DENR-BMB 2016 Atlas Annex 2b independently names Pansipit River and lists Lemery, Taal, Agoncillo and San Nicolas; this does not assign salinity to every reach. Mendoza et al. (2015) reports a 2012 juvenile-fish/gut-content study of the upstream lake-river reach; the species/diet table remains held pending rights review, and no diet or current-presence claim is added.

These sources support a Ternate research lead and source-name variant only; they do not define the full channel or resolve its relationship to the separately named Maragondon River. This is not evidence of fish absence. Full extent, geometry, salinity, fish presence, catchability, access/legal status and reuse terms remain unresolved. GeoNames also lists a Sapang River feature point in Ternate, but the point is about 1.57 km from the nearest segment in the 2013 modelled national stream network. This is too far to confirm a named-channel crosswalk; neither the gazetteer point nor model line is adopted as public geometry.

coverageRules.inventoryMeaning: Named source-backed research leads, not a verified catch list or complete regional waterbody census.

coverageRules.salinityMeaning: Source-context classification only where explicitly supported; unknown remains unknown. Estuary naming alone does not establish a measured brackish value.
coverageRules.administrativeMeaning: Source-described associations; no point-in-polygon or legal boundary claim. Shared waters have one stable research identity and many associations.
coverageRules.speciesMeaning: No names from a water-quality page, landing-center list, stocking report or national checklist become local wild-presence evidence automatically.
coverageRules.completionMeaning: This starter snapshot does not satisfy regional baseline-reviewed status.
